root.name: Ruy Lopez: Retreat Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nb8

overview: After 3.Bb5 Black retreats the knight to b8, losing time. White takes the centre with 4.d4 or 4.c3 and enjoys an easy lead in development. The line is a poor attempt at avoiding theory, not a respected defence.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Bxc6 ideas and castle

black_ideas.idea: Try to catch up in development

gambit.notes: No material is given up in the main line.

soundness.notes: Black has lost a tempo or two; considered poor.

approach.notes: Almost never played by strong players.

level.notes: Easy for White but not recommended for Black.

character.reason: White simply takes the centre and the play is not forcing.

soundness.reason: Black has lost time and White is just better.

structure.reason: White opens the centre with d4.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play it.

level.reason: A dubious line cannot be Beginner.

plans.reason: White profits from the lost tempo.
